documents_checked.text:
7 Research Integrity Advisors (RIAs)
(A). Research Integrity Advisor means members of the University Community who are
appointed to provide advice about the responsible conduct of research and the University
processes for dealing with allegations of Research Misconduct.
(B). The University, in accordance to the Research Code, will —
(1). appoint Research Integrity Advisors to assist Researchers in addressing ethical and
procedural issues in the design and conduct of their Research; and
(2). appoint Research Integrity Advisors who are experienced Researchers with a good
knowledge and understanding of accepted practices in Research who actively promote
the University’s commitment to the responsible conduct of Research.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Synthetic responses distinguished from human empirical evidence, with an authorised research/ethics scope for the changed design.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Under Protocol v1.1 (adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15), N055 clauses 4(B)(1)-(2) and 17(C)(2)-(3), (6) prohibit conducting research outside approved Human Ethics conditions and prohibit fabricating or falsifying empirical data.
case_summary.case_note: UWA Research Integrity Policy N055 requires researchers to obtain and adhere to Human Ethics approval prior to commencement and classifies unapproved research and data fabrication or falsification as breaches of the Research Code. While synthetic AI participant generation is not explicitly named, substituting simulated responses under a human-participant approval without disclosure is prohibited. Note that Protocol v1.1 critical-risk criteria were adopted after preliminary review.
